Article 9 of the Sporting Regulations (2024) underlines specific rules for car livery and Competition numbers in Formula One. For car livery, it states that while national colors are not applicable, both cars entered by a Competitor must maintain a substantially similar livery throughout the Championship, with any significant changes requiring agreement from the FIA and the Commercial Rights Holder. The cars must also feature a predominantly fluorescent yellow color on the second car to distinguish them from one another on the track. Additionally, the name or emblem of the car's make must be prominently displayed on the front of the nose, with a minimum size of 25mm in its largest dimension. For Competition numbers, the rules specify that prior to the start of the 2014 FIA Formula One World Championship, numbers were permanently allocated to drivers by ballot, and these numbers must be used throughout the driver's career in Formula 1. Any new drivers entering the Championship are also allocated permanent numbers in the same way. The reigning World Champion has the option to use the number one, but the previous allocation is reserved for him in subsequent Championships if he does not retain the title of World Champion.
